unfinished.reason: It is a P4 behaviour decision about a stub, and three agents in a row have now declined to encode an answer. I decline too, and I was told not to encode one. What was missing was the question in a form the owner can rule on, so this item is the question, both readings priced against measurements I took, and the measurement that settles each. NOTHING FAILS UNTIL IT LANDS: observe is `raise NotImplementedError`, so no run takes any of the three today.
unfinished.detail:
THE FACT. capacity/api.py::observe's DID IT FIRE line names `at_hard_ceiling` inside a CLOSED block-reason set -- 'targets_off | not_pinned | warmup(observations/1000) | blackout | not_stalled(|improving|/band) | threshold(held/pin_windows) | at_hard_ceiling | dead_rows_unmasked' -- and NOWHERE says whether it tests `cap >= ceiling` or `lift_to(cap) > ceiling`. The two give cap.valve opposite verdicts on a cap just below the ceiling. Reproduced unchanged on the current tree (scratchpad/z/cap_render.py): CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=4095 CAP_VOCAB_START=4095 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 -> 'Gate cap.valve: FIRED (experts 4095/ceiling 4096/settles 1844/one lift -> 4422, vocab 4095/ceiling 4096/one lift -> 4422/mask_dead_rows True ...)'. 4095 + max(8, int(0.08 x 4095)=327) = 4422, which is 326 slots ABOVE the ceiling printed on the same line, on a gate whose sentence is that the arm has room to earn.

READING (A) -- REFUSE THE OVERSHOOT. `at_hard_ceiling` means `lift_to(cap) > ceiling`, and a lift that would land above the ceiling is declined whole.
  WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED: at the shipped CAP_LIFT=0.08 / CAP_LIFT_MIN=8 against the shipped ceiling of 4096, EVERY cap from 3794 to 4095 is permanently frozen -- 302 of the 4095 caps below the ceiling, 7.4%. The largest cap that can still land at or below the ceiling is 3793 (lift_to(3793) = 4096 exactly). At a small ceiling it is nearly total: at FAB_SLOTS=10, caps 3 through 9 all overshoot, so 7 of the 9 caps below the ceiling are frozen. A frozen cap is an arm that is below its ceiling, reports room to earn, and is refused every lift forever -- which is the armed-but-dead reading spine/gate.py exists to refuse, recreated one level down.
  AND IT IS NOT FREE IN THE GATE: cap.valve's `_lift_moves(c)` (`derive.lift_to(c, cap.lift, cap.lift_min) > c`) would have to gain the same test, or the gate prints FIRED for an arm observe will refuse on every flush -- the exact D15 defect that was repaired this round.

READING (B) -- CLAMP TO THE CEILING. The lift is taken as `min(lift_to(cap), ceiling)`; `at_hard_ceiling` then means `cap >= ceiling` and is the block for every LATER lift.
  WHAT IT COSTS: nothing is frozen -- 4095 reaches 4096 in one lift and the top 302 caps become usable. But cap.valve's arithmetic becomes a false equation the moment it lands: 'one lift -> 4422' would print a number the mechanism never takes, which is the class this whole run exists to end. So (B) is only admissible together with printing the clamped value, and with a block reason of its own -- a lift that was partly refused must not enter the histogram as a lift taken, or the C30 shape (a clamp that goes unlogged) arrives through the report instead of through the code.

READING (C) -- TAKE THE OVERSHOOT, which is what the tree as it stands describes (`_lift_moves` is satisfied at 4095, the gate FIRES, and nothing anywhere clamps). The soft cap then exceeds the hard ceiling.
  WHAT DECIDES WHETHER (C) IS ADMISSIBLE AT ALL, and it is a STATIC measurement over the tree rather than a training run: enumerate every reader of the soft cap and check whether each already takes min(soft, hard). I did this for the two that exist. TOK does: `Vocabulary._cap()` is `self.ceiling if self.soft_cap is None else min(int(self.soft_cap), self.ceiling)`, and `at_cap()` is the one predicate, so an overshooting soft cap is harmless there and also INVISIBLE there. FAB does not bind its preallocation to it -- fabric/api.py:1363 says outright that the preallocation ceiling 'is NOT bound by CAP's operating soft cap' -- and its growth clamp lives inside FAB.grow_check, a P4 body. So (C) is not obviously a memory-safety defect, and it IS an honesty defect on every arm: the number an operator reads as the run's capacity would exceed the ceiling the run actually has.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES (A) vs (B), if the static one above rules (C) out. The whole question is worth exactly the top band: 302 of 4096 expert slots, 7.4%, at the shipped levers. So the experiment is a two-arm run at CAP_TARGETS=experts with CAP_FAB_START inside the frozen band (e.g. 3900, FAB_SLOTS=4096) -- refuse vs clamp -- read on the two numbers this project exists for: bits/byte at the end of training (goal A) and the forgetting delta across a resume boundary (goal B). If 7.4% more expert capacity does not move either, (A) is the cheaper answer and the frozen band is a documented, printed fact rather than a defect. If it does, (B) is required and must arrive with its clamp counter. NOTHING IN THE TREE MEASURES THIS TODAY, because observe is a stub.

WHERE THE ANSWER GOES, WHICHEVER IT IS -- all three must move in one commit or the report and the mechanism disagree: (1) `_lift_moves` in capacity/api.py::new_valve, which is at HEAD (line 510 in `git show HEAD:`, NOT 433 as y_capacity N7 says) and which this round did not touch; (2) capacity/api.py::observe's closed block-reason set on its DID IT FIRE line; (3) docs/04_CONTRACT.md's copy of that set, in the CAP section ('`Decision.block_reason` comes from a closed set -- `targets_off | not_pinned | warmup | blackout | not_stalled | threshold | at_hard_ceiling | dead_rows_unmasked`'). I VERIFIED THAT THIS ROUND'S CAP REPAIR IS NEUTRAL BETWEEN THE READINGS: the clause that mentions at_hard_ceiling fires only when `ce >= hard_experts`, and my 3200-cell sweep shows the 4095 corner never reaches it, so nothing I or the previous round wrote has smuggled an answer in.
